purpose: Direct test: does PRISM own pipeline, run on the paper own confirmed-ice craters (F2, F3) with crater-scale circular interior masking, reproduce the paper own CPR>1 & DOP<0.13 finding?
paper: Sinha et al. 2026, npj Space Exploration 2:22
headline_finding: The scale-mismatch hypothesis (whole-PSR averaging washing out a small low-DOP ice patch) is RULED OUT: even restricted to the exact crater circular interior mask on the papers own confirmed-ice craters, PRISM DOP comes back 6x too high (0.79-0.84 vs paper 0.10-0.13). CPR, computed from the same real local mosaic product, IS in close agreement with the papers own numbers for both craters. The gap is specific to DOP, not CPR, pointing to a calibration/acquisition difference rather than a window-size artifact: PRISM only applies bias-centering (no gain-imbalance/phase-orthogonality correction), and the acquisition used here (2020-03-21, found via a blind 602-acquisition scan) is almost certainly not the specific pass the papers authors used (their own acquisition list is in a Supplementary Table not available to this project).
not_yet_resolved: Whether applying full gain-imbalance + phase-orthogonality calibration (not just bias-centering) would close the gap.
Whether a different acquisition/date covering F2/F3 would give a different DOP value (multiple passes may exist; only one was tested).
Whether the papers own DOP formula construction (Stokes S1-S4 from a specific covariance window size/shape) exactly matches PRISMs 5x5 local-window construction.
